newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia politics lose market impact - securities head.
newsitem.headline: Russia politics lose market impact - securities head.

text.p: Foreign investors in Russian securities are no longer worried about political instability and instead are focusing on macroeconomic fundamentals, the head of the country's top securities watchdog said on Wednesday.

Dmitry Vasilyev, chairman of Federal Commission for Capital Markets, told a news conference that Moscow's inflation-busting measures, improved tax-collection rates and rising stock market would cheer Western portfolio investors.
"The political factor no longer influences investors as much as it did in 1996," he said.
Russian inflation slowed in the week ending January 13 to 0.4 percent from 1.1 percent, according to State Statistics Committee estimates released on Wednesday.
The Russian Trading System 24-share index established a new record on Monday despite negative news about President Boris Yeltsin, who was sent to hospital last week.
